This pull request fixes #240 

#### What's Included in This Pull Request

WooCommerce 3.2.0 introduced different handling of Ajax endpoint
URLs, including call to home_url() function, for more info see
woocommerce/woocommerce#16991

This breaks Polylang language detection if language is set from the
directory name in pretty permalinks.

To address this issue we need to add WooCommerce class-wc-ajax.php
file to the white list of the Polylang home_url filter, enabling
home_url() function to return correct URL according to the language
set.

title: Translate Thousand separator and Decimal separator

milestone.description: below items addressed by improvements in 1.0.2 branch https://github.com/hyyan/woo-poly-integration/tree/1.0.2

body:
WooCommerce, Settings has values for Thousand separator and Decimal separator.
These are commonly written differently by language (not by currency). For example, 1 million can be written:
- English:  1,000,000.00
- Spanish: 1.000.000,00
- ISO 31-0: 1 000 000.00  (latest international standards prefer space as thousands separator and reserve use of ',' or '.' to be both acceptable as the decimal separator).

This is primarily by language: in a Spanish article I expect to read numbers in the format 1.000.000,00  and if numbers appear in the wrong format, it is confusing, especially for smaller numbers where it is easier to misread..    1,00  1,000 1.000  1.00 
[Number of decimals, symbol etc, should be up to currency and currency switching mechanism if any but general number format should normally follow locale convention.]

## Price Fields
Implementation looks quite feasible as:
- add to Polylang Languages, String Translations table   pll_register_string ...
- add filters 'wc_get_price_decimal_separator' and 'wc_get_price_thousand_separator'

OR  simply hook the filter and use locale formatting, as WooCommerce does for other number fields, having first set the locale, as below.

## Built-in Attributes
Additionally this number format localisation should also be applied to numeric attributes.
For built-in attributes such as weight, WooCommerce uses wc_format_localized_decimal() which uses localeconv() for decimal point instead of wc_get_price_decimal_separator() and there is no filter, so number representation could be desynchronized between price and other number fields.  
Polylang does add_filter( 'locale' at various points but apparently for this context it is not set.  
There are also separate filters for woocommerce_format_weight and woocommerce_format_dimensions.
It appears this can be fixed by calling         `setlocale(LC_ALL, pll_current_language('locale'));`  then built in fields use locale format...  however note PHP Warning The locale information is maintained per process, not per thread...

## Additional Product Attributes 
For user-defined Products\Attributes the types are only Select and Text, these could be extended to  allow other types such as Number to define where localisation display could be applied.

## Custom Fields / Meta
For other Product Meta there is no standard definition to tell if field is numeric.
It may be possible to implement as an optional feature to localize other values which appear to be numeric... but this may be risky:  instead other plugins should do their own locale formatting for fields where this may be relevant.

title: Synchronisation handling for unknown meta
body:
Many plugins add additional metadata to Products, users also raise support tickets about the handling of the additional data, so the behaviour should clarified and enhanced.

Example components include:

- Yoast SEO (meta keys like '_yoast_%' not synchronised, most fields not desirable to synchronise across translations)
- WP-Lister Lite for eBay and other synchronization tools (mix of field types) 
- Currency switchers with per product/language pricing capability (normally should synchronize).
- Autoposters such as NextScripts: Social Networks Auto-Poster
- Some themes such as Flatsome apparently add data to products 

Normally this data cannot be synchronised, Polylang appears to be not synchronising the data regardless of the options selected (eg Settings, Synchronisation, Custom fields has no effect).   One user appeared to be experiencing the opposite with the Flatsome theme and complained that he could not turn off integration, but did not provide sufficient information to diagnose.

Actually, most of these metas start with `'_'` underscore character.
Polylang `copy_post_metas` skips meta keys matching `is_protected_meta()` which starts by assuming any meta key beginning with '_' is protected [and should not be copied], there is also a filter is_protected_meta to override this. 

One woo-poly user recommended: Currency Switcher for WooCommerce By Algoritmika Ltd 
[free on WordPress.org for 2 extra currencies](https://wordpress.org/plugins/currency-switcher-woocommerce/)   (also authors of Booster for WooCommerce, not sure if this is the same as related Booster feature or not)
This supports setting product level pricing per language which is then saved in wp_postmeta under meta keys such as:
```
_alg_currency_switcher_per_product_regular_price_EUR
_alg_currency_switcher_per_product_sale_price_EUR
_alg_currency_switcher_per_product_regular_price_GBP
_alg_currency_switcher_per_product_sale_price_GBP
```
If used, these should normally be synchronised to the different language versions, one wouldn't expect to have to set the EUR price manually in each language translation.

So how to extend the metas list / fields locker?
Options:

1. - detect Meta keys and add them to "Other Metas" section in the list:  Tricky:  there are a lot, SELECT distinct meta_key FROM wp_postmeta returns >1,000 in my db and as these are not taxonomies there is no definition or grouping of which are valid/relevant.  Also this function gets called a *lot*, not only for the settings screen and on save of product but also for fields locker and other internal functions which test whether meta setting is set.
2. - implement Meta extension panels for particular plugins worth supporting, in the same way as Variables Metas, and open that extension api
3. - in Settings, Meta List, add text boxes for "additional fields to copy" and "additional fields to lock"


For the particular example here, this filter code could be placed in a theme functions.php or plugin to allow these values to be synchronised:

```
/**
 * Polylang meta filter, if true meta item will not be synchronized.
 *
 *
 * @param string      $meta_key Meta key
 * @param string|null $meta_type
 * @return bool True if the key is protected, false otherwise.
 */
function allowSyncCurrencyMeta($protected, $meta_key, $meta_type)
{
    $meta_prefix = '_alg_currency_switcher_per_product_';
    $length = strlen($meta_prefix);
    if (substr($meta_key, 0, $length) === $meta_prefix){
        return false;
    } else {
        return $protected;
    }
}
add_filter( 'is_protected_meta', 'allowSyncCurrencyMeta', 10, 3);
```

added to wiki at https://github.com/hyyan/woo-poly-integration/wiki/Product-Meta-and-Custom-Fields

title: Settings overlap between woo-poly and Polylang
body:
Currently there are various points of confusion about the settings relationships between Polylang and woo-poly which are only partly addressed through the documentation pages.

When changes are made in Polylang admin screens "Languages, Settings", some of these settings are or were silently reset again by woo-poly, other settings take precedence over woo-poly settings and are not reflected in the woo-poly settings page.


## Settings reset in Polylang 

These settings are or were forced set in Polylang on every page load:  you can change in Polylang Languages Settings and in the screen save is successful but on next page load, setting is immediately reset.

### Product Category and Product Tag 
Actually these translation options are no longer forced set in Polylang on every page load, but this is confusing for new users (#180 and https://wordpress.org/support/topic/categories-dont-translate/)  The behaviour change is caused by the removal of manageTaxonomiesTranslation which was forcing all Product Attributes to be translated on every page load, whereas now individual Attributes can be turned on and off for translation in Polylang Settings without being overwritten on next page load.
Possible Options:
- [ ] Remove from woo-poly settings page: instead, register and set on initial plugin activation only, and redirect user to Polylang's Languages, Settings page to manage these settings
- [ ] Synchronize on Save of Polylang settings as well as on save of woo-poly, so latest edit will win.  - [ ] Eliminate the synchronization issue by read/write always from the Polylang setting, so there is no second setting in wpi options which could become unsynchronized.
- [ ] put back manageTaxonomiesTranslation just for Product Categories and Tags which would then be reset on each page load...  as is similarly still done in manageProductTranslation() and manageOrderTranslation()

### Products 
translation is currently forced on and required for woo-poly, there was a support ticket about this, possible solutions may include:
- [ ] only turn on Products translation on initial activation of woo-poly.  If Products translation is later found to be turned off, then deactivate woo-poly or show warning message if Products translation is turned off in Polylang.  This could be added to canActivate() tests
- [ ] disable Products translation checkbox in Polylang settings 


## Settings which independent or conflict between Polylang and woo-Poly

Now covered in [documentation page](https://github.com/hyyan/woo-poly-integration/wiki/Settings-Metas) these woo-poly settings are [mostly] ignored since the Polylang settings are used instead:
- Menu Order (Polylang, Settings, Synchronization, Page order)
- Thumbnail Id (Polylang, Settings, Synchronization, Featured image)
- Comment Status (Polylang, Settings, Synchronization, Comment Status)

Possible solutions may be:

- [ ] Remove these settings from woo-poly
- [ ] Add filter hooks to allow these settings to apply to Products only, whereas the Polylang settings will apply to other Post types.

## Settings which must be set in Polylang

In addition to Products translation which must be on, the setting Languages, Settings, URL Modifications, " The language is set from content" must be not selected, so the same approach should apply.
Simply resetting the value after the user has changed it would just cause confusion, so the option should be disabled or cause woo-poly to deactivate with warning message.

title: Product taxonomies and attributes handling
body:
This release fixes a number of issues around handling of attributes and translations.
In particular:

1. New translations can now use auto-copy of source language, to help save time translating.
   In future a machine translation will be added.
	 Copy option covers Product Title, Short Description and Long Description.
   Also when creating a new product, any missing Product Categories, Tags and Attributes are copied,
   to avoid unexpected problems which occur if a translation is saved with missing term translations.

2. it is now possible to set up the system to allow different types of product attributes
to be synchronised, translated, or independent in each language. The default options will be:
 - Translation and Synchronization Enabled for Product Attributes
 - Synchronization off for Custom Product Attributes

In this case choose how to set up your product attributes as follows:
 - Translated Attribute?  Add in Products\Attributes and turn on Translation in Polylang at:
        Languages\Settings\Custom Taxonomies 
 - Synchronised Attribute? [eg same value in all languages, eg product code, numeric properties] 
				Add in Products\Attributes and leave Translation turned off in Polyang.
 - Different value in each language? add directly to Product as a Custom Product Attribute

* Enh: synchronisation for Custom Product Attributes and Global Product Attributes can now be 
       turned on and off independently in 
			 Settings\WooPoly, Metas List, Attributes Metas, Custom Product Attributes.
       The fields locker is unlocked for the attribute types which are not synchronized.
* Fix: Global Product Attributes can now be individually configured in Polylang:  
			 When Settings\WooPoly Translation attributes is checked then attributes appear in Polylang:
       Languages\Settings\Custom Taxonomies lists the individual taxonomies 
			 Previously all attributes translation were forced on: now they can be selectively turned on and off.  This means that there is no longer any need to create dummy translations for untranslateable values such as reference codes and numeric fields.  Fixes #127.

CHANGE: new Product Attributes are no longer automatically enabled for translation,
       After creating new Attribute, enable Translation in Polylang if needed by checking:
			 Languages\Settings\Custom Taxonomies 
* Enh: Missing Term Translations are now added by default. Fixes #72
			 Applies to Products\Categories, Products\Tags, Products\Attributes 
       Previously missing term translations caused
* Fixes: #148 WooCommerce3 product_visibility is now a taxonomy not a meta item  
* Fixes: #153 Fields locker doesn't correctly lock Product Attributes of type Select
